statement: Fix D, the bounded scaled portions of the contour families of Lemma 4.1, and a fixed lower radius r∗ > 0. Let p0(s) be a suffi- ciently high polynomial truncation of b p(s). For some fixed L and outer ball in (4.38), for every p ∈ Bout s and every choice of outgoing data in (4.37) at the artificial exits, the normal- ized stationary problem on either contour family has a unique solution in the perturbative UNIQUENESS OF TANGENT FLOWS 45 neighborhood. For each fixed contour, the solution operator is jointly holomorphic in p and an independent complex trace remainder δg ∈ TB for p ∈ Bout s and ∥δg∥TB < cholB−4, with a fixed chol > cexit. Hence a chosen p-dependent datum gives a holomorphic solution when δg(p) is holomorphic into that fixed trace space and remains in the stated trace ball on Bout s . Smooth contour families with smooth prescribed data give smooth solution families. Every allowed solution lies in the growth-weighted augmented ball ∥(u, λ) − (uapp, λapp)∥XB ≤ CpreB−4 , where the fixed Cpre is chosen before B. In the preceding strip norms its correction satisfies W(z) ≤ CDB−4 (1 + |z|)2.2 . (4.39) Its compact and conical correction is O(B−4). In particular on |z| ≍ B its discrepancy from circular data is O(B−1.8). The same conclusions hold in one such neighborhood along curtailment, path, and exit-data homotopies that retain the fixed lower radius and (4.37), with the just stated regularity of the data for the corresponding family-regularity conclusion. This includes the first fixed-radius height turn, but not the subsequent shrinking height turns. Fixed finite parameter derivatives on Bs and the prescribed smooth contour derivatives have only polynomial losses in B and |s|−1.
